candidate.de: Ein traditioneller Wallfahrtsprozession von der Dorf.
candidate.en: a traditional pilgrimage procession from the village.
candidate.venue: the church of Gospa od Carskog Polja in the field below the village (Gospa od Carskog Polja / Our Lady of Čara Field, 14th century, Baroque style, with an impressive marble altar and a coloured English bas-relief in alabaster depicting four scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary, an unusual piece of English workmanship in this remote Dalmatian setting). Every year on 25 July (the feast of Sveti Jakov — St James’s Day) the church is the centre of a traditional pilgrimage procession from the village. The church is in the field of Carsko Polje below the village, planted almost entirely with vines, and the village’s winegrowers have built their large cooperative wine cellar here, where the celebrated Pošip white wine is produced. The cellar is located near the small road that connects Čara with the southern coast bays of Zavalatica, Žitna, and Čavića Luka. The port of Zavalatica on the southern coast was historically the export harbour for Čara’s wine — barrels were carried down from the village to the bay for loading onto ships. Today, Zavalatica is a small tourist resort with apartments, cafes and restaurants, as is the nearby bay of Žitna.)
